# `utils/MemoryIntegration.js`

> **Source:** `editor/js/utils/MemoryIntegration.js`

MemoryIntegration.js - Wires up off-heap memory to editor/engine systems Integrates OffHeapMemoryManager with: - Particle snapshot system (large frame buffers → WASM/Worker) - Editor history (old undo entries → IDB) - Asset cache (loaded assets → Worker memory) - Profiler timeline (frame history → off-heap)

## Functions

### `async initMemoryIntegration(gpuDevice = null)`

Initialize memory integration

### `async rebindMemoryIntegration(gpuDevice = null)`

Rebind the GPU tier without replacing CPU/off-heap persistence state.

### `async prepareMemoryIntegrationRebind(gpuDevice = null)`

Stage a replacement GPU tier without publishing it before the recovery commit.

### `getMemoryPressure()`

Get current memory pressure (0-1)

### `shouldOffload()`

Check if we should offload to off-heap storage

### `async storeParticleFrame(frameIndex, frameData)`

Store particle frame in off-heap memory Large frames (>100KB) go to worker memory

### `async retrieveParticleFrame(frameIndex)`

Retrieve particle frame from off-heap storage

### `async freeParticleFrame(frameIndex)`

### `async archiveHistoryEntry(index, entry)`

Store old history entry to IDB when memory pressure is high

### `async retrieveHistoryEntry(index)`

Retrieve archived history entry from IDB

### `async cacheAsset(uuid, data)`

Store large asset in worker memory

### `async retrieveCachedAsset(uuid, asText = false)`

Retrieve cached asset from worker memory

### `storeProfilerFrames(frames)`

Store profiler frame batch in WASM memory

### `async getMemoryStats()`

Get comprehensive memory stats

### `formatMemoryForProfiler(stats)`

Format memory stats for profiler display

## Notes & Examples

### Editor Extension System

The editor supports extensions via the same Plauna component system as apps. Extensions can add panels, tools, menu items, and hooks into the engine. They run with elevated 'editor' capability granting access to the scene graph, asset database, and build pipeline.

**Example: Editor extension adding a custom panel**
```js
import { Extension } from 'editor/core/Extension.js';
import { Panel } from 'editor/ui/Panel.js';

class TerrainEditor extends Extension {
  id = 'terrain-editor';
  capabilities = ['editor', 'scene'];
  
  activate(context) {
    // Add menu item
    context.menus.add('Tools/Terrain', () => this.open());
    
    // Register tool
    context.tools.register('terrain', {
      icon: 'mountain',
      onSelect: (entity) => this.edit(entity)
    });
  }
  
  open() {
    this.panel = new Panel({
      title: 'Terrain Editor',
      content: this.buildUI()
    });
    context.workspace.addPanel(this.panel);
  }
  
  edit(entity) {
    const terrain = entity.get(TerrainComponent);
    this.panel.bind(terrain);
  }
}

editor.extensions.register(TerrainEditor);
```
